DrainageAreaClass.notes: Watershed drainage area class. Breakpoints 10 and 100 km2 are fixed constants.
DrainageAreaClass.rationale: Drainage area is the primary scaling variable for channel geometry, discharge and assemblage composition. 10 km2 separates headwaters from wadeable small streams; 100 km2 separates small streams from larger wadeable rivers. Both are conventional round-number breaks in NRSA and NHDPlus practice, not sample quantiles.

ChannelSlopeClass.notes: Reach channel slope class. Breakpoints 0.5 and 2 percent are fixed constants.
ChannelSlopeClass.rationale: Channel slope controls stream power, substrate sorting and channel type. 0.5 and 2 percent are the conventional low gradient, moderate and steep breaks used in Rosgen-family and Montgomery-Buffington channel typing. National median slope is near 0.13 percent, so this ladder is eligible in roughly half of L3 ecoregions; it is screened where it qualifies and excluded with a recorded reason where it does not.

ElevationClass.notes: Mean watershed elevation class. Breakpoints 300 and 1000 m are fixed constants.
ElevationClass.rationale: Elevation proxies thermal regime, precipitation phase and growing season length. 300 and 1000 m are conventional lowland, upland and montane breaks. Within a single ecoregion this often collapses to two populated classes, which the eligibility screen handles.

referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 17 curves are fitted to least-disturbed stations of this ecoregion. 7 curves are fitted to this ecoregion's own streams under the documented regional screen, which relaxes agriculture only. 5 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 1 carries the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 1 carries the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 5 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Measurement-precision floor. The Functioning core of this two-sided curve spans 0.374 Std. Units (8.15 to 8.53 Std. Units at n = 25), narrower than 0.4 Std. Units, 2 times the metric's documented measurement precision of 0.2 Std. Units, so band assignments inside it would present measurement noise as condition classes and the metric is withheld at the build under rule CURVE-09. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.

Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance.
